title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context

cost.compute_notes: arXiv PDF (18 pp) read: main text, Tables 2-7, Appendix A; Appendix B/C (sample outputs, full prompts) not read. GSM-IC repo at commit 0c1da13552afcc5d995d6f1ad5288417cb110246: GSM-IC_2step.json (26.1 MB, sha256 0a8c2ae7991feeef...), GSM-IC_mstep.json (22.9 MB, 152897a5df9ff1aa...), gsm8k_validation.jsonl (283 kB). Data kept outside the KB (regenerable with fetch_cmd). No model outputs are released. g1-g5 run in seconds; g2 known-answer test about a minute.

triggers: do irrelevant sentences hurt LLM math reasoning
macro accuracy all variants solved depends on number of variants
selection on success regression to the mean benchmark construction
neutral perturbation control for distractor studies

claims.statement: Among base problems solved by the baseline prompts, no more than 18% are consistently solved across all types of irrelevant information (macro accuracy; best overall macro, with self-consistency, 45%), showing the models are easily distracted.
claims.scope: code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003, GSM-IC-4K (4,000 variants sampled uniformly from 58,052; on average 40 per base, about 10-60), 100 base problems.

quantities.name: macro_accuracy_ltm_gsmic4k
quantities.unit: share of 100 bases with every sampled variant correct

quantities.name: gsmic_variants_per_base
quantities.baseline: 8 templates x 10 role names x 8 numbers; a uniform 4K sample gives a mean of 40 per base

quantities.name: predicted_macro_ltm_at_10_variants
quantities.ci: 0.293-0.406 (90%, binomial redraw of the printed macro)
quantities.baseline: printed 4K value 0.18; predicted on the full 58K set 0.043 (0.016-0.090)

our_assessment.why: Macro accuracy is an all-of-m criterion, so its value is set by m, the number of variants sampled per base, as much as by the model. A Beta model of per-base accuracy, pinned to each row's printed micro and macro, says LTM's 18% would be about 35% if each base had 10 variants and about 4% on the full 58K dataset, with the model unchanged. Known-answer test (g2): with exchangeable variants the method recovers the true full-set and m = 10 macro within 0.01-0.02; with template-level heterogeneity it under-predicts at small m, so the m = 10 figures are if anything conservative. The qualitative claim (few bases are fully robust) stands; the number 18% belongs to GSM-IC-4K's sampling density and must not be compared with a macro accuracy computed at another m.

claims.statement: Model performance is dramatically decreased when irrelevant information is included: e.g. code-davinci-002 COT from 95.0% on the base problems to 72.4% micro accuracy on GSM-IC-4K.
claims.scope: The 100 base problems were selected from 1,000 GSM8K training problems as those 'that can be correctly solved by at least one of the prompting techniques'; the same COT prompt scores 60.3% on all 1,000 (Table 5).

quantities.name: zero_distraction_micro_under_selection_null
quantities.unit: predicted accuracy with an added sentence that has NO effect
quantities.baseline: printed 0.724, reproduced exactly at k = 2.28; k = 2-4 gives 0.68-0.74

quantities.name: variants_with_question_rewritten
quantities.unit: share of GSM-IC variants that change the base text beyond inserting one sentence
quantities.baseline: 32 of 100 bases, usually all their variants; e.g. pronoun -> name, and 'How much will be Jewel gain' -> 'How much will Jewel gain'

quantities.name: in_topic_minus_off_topic_micro_cot
quantities.baseline: the identified part: selection cannot create a difference between two sentence types on the same bases

our_assessment.why: The size of the headline drop is not identified as distraction. Bases were chosen for having been solved, so ANY change to the prompt is a fresh draw that regresses toward each problem's true success rate. In a null world with no distraction at all, per-problem heterogeneity of the size the paper's own micro/macro numbers imply (k = 2-4, g1) plus selection on COT success predicts 68-74% with-sentence accuracy; the printed 72.4% is inside that range (g4). The weaker selection rule ('any of four techniques') cannot be the operative one, since it predicts a base accuracy near 70%, not 95%. A second confound sits inside the treatment: 31.4% of variants also reword the question (g5), usually disambiguating it. The missing condition is a neutral extra sentence on the same bases. What IS identified is the contrast between sentence types on the same bases: in-topic sentences cost 17.6 points more than off-topic ones for COT, and off-topic 80.7% is ABOVE the zero-distraction null, so off-topic sentences may cost nothing. A pre-registered local test of this decomposition is in reanalysis/PLAN.md.

checked.how: curl the raw files; python reanalysis/g1_macro_classsize.py <dir>; python reanalysis/g5_question_edits.py
checked.result: 58,052 variants over 100 bases (60 two-step), class sizes 192-640; role/number/topic labels as documented. The GSM-IC-4K sample used in the paper is NOT released, nor any model output, so no table cell can be recomputed. 31.4% of variants carry question edits beyond the inserted sentence (Appendix A step 4).

artifacts.fetch_cmd: for f in GSM-IC_2step.json GSM-IC_mstep.json gsm8k_validation.jsonl; do curl -sL -o $f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-research-datasets/GSM-IC/0c1da13552afcc5d995d6f1ad5288417cb110246/$f; done

relations.why: Both find that what distracts is plausible, related content: in-topic sentences hurt far more than off-topic ones here; real passages hurt and word salad does not there.
Both read a context manipulation's effect off a comparison without a content-free control of matched length and position.

open_questions: Pre-registered local decomposition (reanalysis/PLAN.md, qwen3.5:4b): selection effect, neutral-sentence drop, content-specific drop. Running 2026-10-17.
Do bases with rewritten questions (32 of 100) behave differently? Exploratory, from the same local run.
Ask the authors for the GSM-IC-4K sample ids and per-variant outputs; with them c2 becomes testable on codex itself (now deprecated) -- probably not obtainable.
